column1: DENGUE CASE REPORTING During  the  34th  week,  1802  suspected  dengue  cases were reported across all 26 districts, compared to 2613 cases  in  the  previous  week,  reflecting  31%  decrease. The  Western  Province  accounted  for  52.6%  of  total cases,  with the  Colombo  Municipal  Council (CMC) contributing 3.8%, the rest of Colombo District 20.7%, Gampaha  District  20.5%,  and  Kalutara  District  7.5%. Outside the Western Province, notable case contributions were reported from Kandy (10.4%), Galle (5.1%),  Kegalle (4.6%),  Ratnapura (3.2%),  Matara (3.2%), Kurunegala (2.7%),  Hambantota (2.4%), Anuradhapura (2.3%), and Badulla (2.3%). WEEKLY DISTRIBUTION OF DENGUE PATIENTS in 2024, 2025 and 2026   Source: NaDSys – National Dengue Surveillance System HIGH RISK MOH AREAS  As presented in Table 2, during the 34th week of 2026, 50 Medical Officer of Health (MOH) areas were identified as high-risk, including 3 newly flagged areas (highlighted in light red in Table 2). Previously classified 29 high-risk MOH areas in week 33, were not identified as high-risk in the 34th week of 2026 (Table 2). MIDNIGHT TOTAL OF DENGUE PATIENT ADMISSIONS *  After  incorporating  delayed  hospital  reports,  the average midnight total for the 33rd week increased from 809 to 813. In the 34th week of 2026, the average midnight total of dengue  patients  across  73  sentinel  hospitals  was  641. Compared  to  the  previous  week,  in  the  34th  week,  17 hospitals  reported  an increase,  while  46  reported  a decrease.
